key_insight: IV-CoT separates structural planning from appearance rendering by using an implicit visual reasoning space, helping text-to-image models follow complex prompts more faithfully. This improves object counts, spatial relations, attribute bindings, and coarse layouts without requiring explicit step-by-step text reasoning.
problem_solved: The paper addresses poor structure-aware prompt following in unified multimodal large language models for text-to-image generation, especially when prompts require correct counts, layouts, object relationships, and attribute assignments.
method: Introduces Implicit Visual Chain-of-Thought (IV-CoT), a latent visual reasoning mechanism for planning image structure before final rendering.
Decouples structural planning from appearance generation to reduce entanglement in a single conditioning stream.
Uses visual latent reasoning to better preserve prompt constraints such as spatial arrangement, object binding, and overall composition.
impact: This matters because it can make text-to-image systems more reliable for real-world creative and design workflows where prompt fidelity is critical. For practitioners, it offers a pathway to generate images with stronger control over structure without sacrificing generative quality.

paper_title: IV-CoT: Implicit Visual Chain-of-Thought for Structure-Aware Text-to-Image Generation
paper_authors: Zixuan Li, Haokun Lin, Yicheng Xiao, Zhiwei Li, Xinyang Song
